episodes.183627: Scattered storms developed across the high terrain of western New Mexico during the early afternoon hours. One of these storms moved northeast through Albuquerque producing penny to quarter sized hail in the southwest and central part of the city.
episodes.183834: The presence of a strong upper level jet overhead paired with daytime heating fueled showers and thunderstorms across portions of southwest Colorado. One storm in southwest Montrose County produced hail that was between 0.75 and 1.00 inches near Paradox.
episodes.184879: A weak cold front helped trigger scattered showers along the Lake Ontario shoreline of western New York. A brief waterspout formed within these showers just offshore of Wilson.
episodes.185580: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce funnel cloud southeast of Charlotte Beach in Charlotte County.
episodes.185695: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a 62 mph wind gust just east of Livingston.
episodes.185787: Scattered thunderstorms developed over portions of Northwest Kansas. These storms mainly moved over Decatur, Sheridan, Norton, and Graham counties. These storms produced pea to quarter sized hail in Decatur and Sheridan counties, with the largest hail falling near Hoxie, Kansas.
episodes.185942: A warm and moist airmass presided over the Florida peninsula and local waters, with weak convergent flow over the Gulf of Mexico waters leading to the development of showers.
episodes.186081: A 59 mph wind gust measured in Jefferson County.
episodes.189403: A surface trough axis moved southward across Lake Erie during the afternoon and early evening of the 19th. Low-level convergence and horizontal wind shear along the surface trough axis contributed to the development of a waterspout that accompanied showers and thunderstorms attendant to the trough axis. These showers and storms occurred in an environment comprised of weak effective bulk shear and weak lake-induced instability as Lake Erie was warm relative to overlying air and thus the primary source of heat, moisture, and instability.
